{{Short description|American biologist (1938–2019)}}
{{for|the architectural historian|Samuel D. Gruber}}

'''Samuel H. Gruber''' (May 13, 1938 – April 18, 2019) was a [[shark]] biologist and founder of the [[American Elasmobranch Society]]. He was a professor at the [[University of Miami]]'s Rosenstiel School for Marine and Atmospheric Science and the founder of the [[Bimini]] Biological Field Station Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biminisharklab.com/|title=Shark Research &#124; Bimini Biological Field Station - Shark Lab|website=Biminisharklab.com}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Dr. Gruber hailed originally from Brooklyn, New York, and grew up in south Florida.  He entered college in 1956, studying first at [[Emory University]] and then earning his B.S. in zoology from the [[University of Miami]].  He followed up in quick succession with his M.S. and Ph.D. in marine science from the then called Institute of Marine and Atmospheric Science, again at the University of Miami.  He held several positions there and completed a postdoctoral fellowship at the Max-Planck Institute for Behavioral Physiology, [[Pöcking|Seewiesen]], Germany, where he was a behavioral researcher under [[List of Nobel laureates|Nobel Laureate]] Professor Dr. [[Konrad Lorenz]].

== Research ==
Gruber was a recognized authority on shark science,<ref name=AP2004>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna5560773|title=Researchers tout shark repellent|website=Nbcnews.com|access-date=8 November 2021}}</ref> having completed 49 Atlantic research cruises and 170 scientific publications.  He has specialized in shark behavior, anatomy, sensory systems, tracking,{{citation needed|date=April 2015}} and [[shark repellent]]s.<ref>

== Institutions ==
In 1983 Gruber founded the [[American Elasmobranch Society]] (AES).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.elasmo.org/aesofficers.php |title=The American Elasmobranch Society |access-date=2009-08-07 |archive-date=2009-05-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090530034721/http://elasmo.org/aesofficers.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> The AES is the world's largest association of shark and ray scientists.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=http://discovery.blogs.com/shark_conservation/|title=Discovery Channel: Shark Conservation|date=15 August 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090815071451/http://discovery.blogs.com/shark_conservation/|access-date=8 November 2021|archive-date=2009-08-15}}</ref> Gruber established the now world-famous "Shark Lab" in 1990, after successfully battling malignant lymphoma.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www6.miami.edu/sharklab/ |title=Bimini Biological Field Station - shark research & marine biology internships |access-date=2008-02-02 |archive-date=2006-09-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060901103601/http://www6.miami.edu/sharklab/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>  The next year he helped found and served as the first chair of the [[International Union for Conservation of Nature]] (IUCN) Shark Specialist Group.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cms.iucn.org/|title=IUCN - Home|date=16 August 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080816213232/http://cms.iucn.org/|access-date=8 November 2021|archive-date=2008-08-16}}</ref>

== Media appearances ==
In August 2008, Gruber appeared on the [[History (U.S. TV channel)|History Channel]]'s documentary series, [[Evolve (TV series)|''Evolve'']] episode 4, entitled "Sex". Gruber has also made several appearances on television programs for [[Discovery Channel]]'s [[Shark Week]], including an appearance in ''Sharkman'', in which [[Michael Rutzen]] attempts to learn how to hypnotize sharks, and in the show ''10 Deadliest Sharks'', where he describes the behavior of [[lemon shark]]s. He also made an appearance in 2008 on the Discovery Channel ''[[MythBusters]]'', also during Shark week.<ref name="auto"/>
